title: Sweet three-way harmony at Pete Herman's Ringside and the Mellon Pickers
summary: He recalls a tight non-reading band at the Ringside, and Henry Wilder's Mellon Pickers.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Mm-hmm . Harry was playing alto sax. And they had one of the sweetest bands I ever heard gotten together in this town at the, Pete Hyman's ringside. Freddie Newman on piano. They had, I think Chink was playing bass with me, if I remember right. I know Harry and Sidney Reedman. Boy, but they had some three-way harmony with that group, Paul, was out of this world. That's one of the only bands I can remember, Dixieland bands, where you could hear three-way harmony. You know, most of them, they just go off and they play for themselves. But these fellas were really tight. Yeah, the group that was tight, man. Played some nice stuff.
I don't think they would be reading much, either.

They weren't reading. They'd all come from here. That's what I'm telling you. And boy, they had guys used to come around there from all over and sit out and listen at that band. And the way they had that ringside pattern, the acoustics in that band was like they were playing in a jewel box. Perfect. They had the whole ringside patterned, you know. And man, the sound in there was perfect. You know, they had a good band in there, too. Henry Wilder had a good band in there with the Mellon Pickers. Raymond played with them. Raymond was with them there.
Who else was in the Mellon Pickers?
I don't remember too many of them.
I think Raymond's got a picture. Yeah, he oughta have. Yeah.
I know Raymond was with them and Henry. And I think, uh, I can't call this trumpet fella's name. I know him and I can't recall his name. Heavisett Italian fella. I can't think of his name.
